_comment: The single-path form. Unchanged, and still the right shape whenever
one host runs everything: this repository lives here, and any executor
may run jobs in it.
One logical slug, two hosts. The slug is still the only thing anyone
names -- Discord supplies a slug and never a path -- and the
repository reservation is still keyed on the slug, so ONE job runs in
this repository at a time no matter which host takes it.
`placements` is EXHAUSTIVE: an executor not listed here is not
eligible, and its jobs wait rather than running against a directory
that means something else on that machine. Do not also set a top-level
`absolutePath`; the schema refuses both forms at once rather than
deciding which wins.
`preferredExecutorId` is a preference, never a pin. While that host is
live it takes the work; once it is not, the other placed hosts become
eligible again, because one host being off should not mean one
repository being dead.
`enabled: false` on a placement takes one host out of rotation without
deleting the path you will want back.
Watch-only. This repository exists in the allowlist so it can be
OBSERVED through the read-only `gh` surface, and for no other reason.
`allowJobs: false` is what keeps those two permissions apart. Watching
is a read; running a job hands a real agent edit capability in a
working tree. Before this flag, adding a GitHub mapping so a
repository could be watched also made it a job target.
It has no path at all, on any host, and needs none: `/job submit`
refuses it before a job row is ever created.
